report.summary: An invoice-themed Word document launched hidden, base64-encoded PowerShell on host WS-ACC-14 to download and execute an external script from an IP address previously associated with a confirmed phishing campaign.

claims.text: Reported by EDR on host WS-ACC-14 (AL-): Office application spawned PowerShell.
Microsoft Word (winword.exe) spawned PowerShell (pid 3300) running as user CORP\mlee from C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE.
PowerShell was executed with a hidden window and a base64-encoded command line.
The decoded PowerShell command line contained a download cradle targeting http://203.0.113.50/a.ps1.
PowerShell made a network connection to external destination 203.0.113.50:80 (update.invalid-cdn.example).
External IP 203.0.113.50 and domain update.invalid-cdn.example were seen in past true positive alert PA-2026-1003 involving Word macro launching hidden encoded PowerShell.

recommended_next_steps: Isolate host WS-ACC-14 immediately to prevent further lateral movement or payload execution.
Collect process memory and disk artifacts from host WS-ACC-14 for forensic analysis.
Block external IP address 203.0.113.50 and domain update.invalid-cdn.example at the perimeter firewall and proxy.
Hunt across the environment for other hosts that received invoice_2211.docm or similar invoice-themed attachments.
Tune EDR detection rules to alert on Office applications spawning shell processes with hidden windows or encoded parameters.
